chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding
a man performing Tamattu' who forgot to shorten his hair until he entered the state of Ihram for Hajj, he said: He seeks forgiveness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: He entered the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.مُتَمِّعٍ: A pilgrim performing Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: To shorten (specifically referring to trimming hair)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a Mutamatti' forgets to cut their hair before entering Ihram?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the omission of the essential act of Qasr (trimming hair) before entering Ihram for Tamattu' Hajj is treated as a minor defect rather than a nullifier, requiring only Istighfar. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of leniency in cases of forgetfulness (Nasi), distinguishing it from intentional omission which might require a sacrifice (Hady). The hadith underscores the importance of spiritual purification alongside ritual compliance in the performance of Hajj.
